roundBegin.say: You there, the one the stranger brought in. You can't walk about unarmed.
Come and see me first. I've a gift for you.

roundOffer.say: Every keeper in Overlook has a gift for a newcomer. Hear them all.
Learn the Tack's horse and the Harbourmaster's ship. Then choose a house.

roundWeaponsmith.say: Pick one blade and one to shoot with. Both are my gift.
Plain steel's always here. The finer pieces change with the day.

roundArmorsmith.say: Head, body, arms, legs. Here's a plain set of all four, on me.
Wear them when you can. Plain still stops a blade.

roundMage.say: Vestiges wash up sealed tight. Here's one, to start you off.
Hand it back and I'll open it. Whatever's inside is yours.

roundVault.say: I've laid a cloak in your vault. Take it out, it's yours.
Bring me what you cannot carry. I count it in, and count it out.

roundTailor.say: Dyes for your armour, emblems for your name. Harbour Blue, on the house.
Wear it proudly. Grey gets you mistaken for the Tithe.

roundTack.say: First horse is on me. This Bay's never thrown anyone.
Barding too, to dress them in. A good mount spares your legs.

roundMail.say: There's a letter for you already. Sign for it, and it's yours.
Whatever you drop and leave behind finds its way to my shelves.

roundHarbour.say: The sea gave you back, then. The Sloop at the quay is yours.
There's a Tithe hulk moored offshore. Put a ball in it, then come home.

rideBegin.say: When you've a horse under you, ride down to my stall. A ship's waiting.

sailHome.say: Back afloat, and that hulk the worse for it. You'll do.

houseBegin.say: You'll hear all three of us. Start with the loudest. Me.

houseStorm.say: Arlo Kestrel. We keep the Storm, and the Storm keeps nobody waiting.
You've met one of its hounds already, I think. Pledge here, and climb.

houseLamp.say: We mend what the sea breaks, child, and we keep the lamps lit.
Pledge with us and you'll walk the shingle where the ships are lost.

houseVeil.say: Sable. That is all the name you will get.
We read what the Tithe writes. Pledge here, and you will read it too.

stormBegin.say: The Tithe have taken our storm-glass from the Old Beacon. Pell went after it.
Climb the Old Beacon on the Downs. I'll speak to you on the wind.

stormBeacon.say: Empty racks, and Pell's knife in the floor. He'd never leave that behind.

stormCamp.say: Their tracks go down to the barns. Search them. Gather Brineglass too.

stormGlass.say: That's ours. Feel it hum? Now climb, as high as you can.

stormHold.say: Plant it on the High Downs and don't let go. They'll come for it.

stormLost.say: They knocked it down. Plant it again, and this time hold it.

stormCalled.say: Hold it up. Stand still. Let the storm decide.

stormHorde.say: There. It's in you, and here comes the Tithe. Call it, and keep calling.

stormOverrun.say: Up. The storm's still yours. Get back to the Downs and call it.

stormSpent.say: That was the storm with nothing holding it. It won't run that free again.
But it's yours now, and it'll answer whenever you call.

stormTrail.say: Arlo? It's done. Don't come looking for me.
That was Pell, on the wind.
And Grey Point Light is burning with lightning. Only a caller can do that.

stormQuicken.say: Pell's tracks run with Tithe boots, toward their camp. You'll need quicker feet.
Let the storm into your legs. We call it Quicken.

stormLedger.say: No Pell. But their tally names a ship taking our lightning rods to sea.

stormSea.say: Take a ship west. Find a grey sail. Beat her any way you can.

stormIsle.say: Their crew talked. The rods went ashore on an isle the Tithe guard.

stormRods.say: Half our rods, wrapped in Tithe cloth. Take one. Shape the storm your way.

stormRiders.say: The rest rode up the river road with Pell. Run under my storm.

stormSlow.say: It's blown out. Back to Weir Mill, and I'll call you another.

stormPell.say: I lit Grey Point for them. They said it would pay my family's tenth.
Corvane's counting the storm, Arlo. He means to sell it back to us.
Come home, Pell. And you, take this. We call it Arc Lash.

stormGround.say: They staked rods round the Old Stones to pull the storm down for him.
Strike them as the storm walks in. West, then north, east and south.

stormWrong.say: Wrong way round. West, north, east, south. Start again from the sea.

stormGrounded.say: The rods are cold. Corvane has nothing left to count.

stormMaw.say: The High Assessor waits in the Maw of the Shallows. End his counting.

stormFalls.say: Everything is owed. Even the storm. Even me.

stormCorvane.say: Not anymore. Bring the storm home.

stormHome.say: The racks are full again. Pell's mending them himself, and won't take help.
You climbed before you walked. That's a Stormcaller.
Thank you. I won't sell the sky again. Not for anything.

lampBegin.say: Someone has stolen our Beacon's lens, child. The light reaches half as far.
A ship broke on Shingle Landing. Go. Our lamps will carry my voice.

lampShingle.say: Are you real? There were lights ashore. We steered for them. Then rocks.
False lights, lit where our Beacon should have reached. Keep that boy safe.

lampFold.say: Ewe Fold will take him in. Ride with him there, and keep him close.

lampWalk.say: Stay close? The ones who lit those lights could be watching.

lampMount.say: Get up on your horse. I'm not riding out there alone.

lampBarrows.say: Those are our barrows. That's where the false lights burn. Keep him moving.

lampSafe.say: They were waiting for us to break. I heard them laughing.
He's safe now. Go back up, and put out every false light.

lampDark.say: Dark again. Their purses hold Tithe silver, paid out at Gullwing in the Vale.

lampHorde.say: Here come the rest. The light's in you now. Burn them all.

lampOverrun.say: They dragged you down. Get up, and bring the light back to the barrows.

lampSunwell.say: Enough. It won't pour out of you like that again.
Now hang a sun where you stand. All beneath it heal. That's the Sunwell.

lampMend.say: The Tithe beat Gullwing's people for seeing wreckers paid. They'll be back.
The light will close your own wounds now. We call that Mend.

lampLost.say: They got to the wounded. Go back, and hold this time.

lampPay.say: The wreckers' ship waits offshore for its pay. Sail west and find it.

lampCove.say: Their captain bought his neck with a cove. Whatever they took is buried there.

lampLens.say: Their hoard, but not our lens. Choose what the light becomes in your hands.

lampHulks.say: Their tally says it was sold at the Saltbreaker Hulks, on the Moors.

lampBuyer.say: Lamplighters. The Tithe bought your lens fairly. Go home, little candle.

lampDawn.say: Nothing stolen is bought fair. Burn their dark away, child. That's Dawnflare.

lampGrey.say: Grey Point burns for the Tithe. Set it true: red, white, green, then gold.

lampWrong.say: Not that one. Red, then white, then green, then gold.

lampLit.say: Grey Point burns true. Its gold has found a door where none should be.

lampTomb.say: The Reeve answered to someone in the Pearl Tomb. Our lens is there.

lampFalls.say: The Tithe will light its own lamps.

lampReeve.say: Then they will burn without us. Bring the lens home.

lampHome.say: The lens is back on the Beacon. Every ship at sea will see it.
Tobin watched it light from Ewe Fold. You light the way now.

veilBegin.say: Your name was in the Tithe's book before you washed ashore.
I want that page. Their collectors carry tallies through Saltgrass. Follow one.

veilTail.say: There. That collector. Keep him in sight, and never close.

veilNoticed.say: He felt you there. Let him settle, then try again.

veilRuin.say: He left his tallies in the ruin. Lift every one before he comes back.

veilTallies.say: Three bundles, nineteen tallies, and your name on every one. The book is close.

veilAdit.say: Its reckoner works in the Chalk Adit. Get there with no eye on you.

veilSeen.say: They saw you. Get clear, and try again.

veilUnseen.say: You came unseen. Good. The reckoner has gone to Moorhold, on the Moors.

veilHorde.say: They found the adit empty, and they're coming. Give them all of the dark.

veilOverrun.say: They had you. Get back to the adit, and let the dark out again.

veilRaven.say: Enough. The dark won't come that freely again.
Take it with you. Its raven wounds them, and heals you.

veilDaggers.say: His guards hold Moorhold, too many to walk past. So do not walk.
Throw. We call them Dusk Daggers.

veilShip.say: The reckoner put to sea with the book, aboard a Tithe ship.

veilSea.say: Sail west and take a Tithe ship's deck. Search it for the book.

veilIsle.say: No book aboard, but their log names the reckoner's isle.

veilLedger.say: No book here. Only his ledger, in a cipher Wren can read.
Choose what the dark becomes in your hands. Wren waits at Vale Mouth.

veilWren.say: You're the one Thule couldn't drown. Keep up, and keep quiet.

veilMount.say: On your horse. We ride hard, or we don't ride.

veilOrchard.say: Collectors work this orchard. Head down, and carry something.

veilHalf.say: His ledger says half your debt's already paid. By someone in Overlook.
Interesting. Vanish now, and follow the book. Like this.

veilMarks.say: The ledger puts his chest at Valeguard. It opens to four marks.
Touch them as he counts: tithe, debt, interest, then fee.

veilWrong.say: Wrong. Tithe, then debt, then interest, then fee. He counts the tithe first.

veilOpened.say: Empty, but for a slip in his hand. One word: Grotto.

veilGrotto.say: Kraken's Grotto, then. The book went down there, and its keeper never leaves.

veilKeeper.say: Your name stays written. The book remembers.

veilBook.say: The book. Your name's in it. I read no further.

veilHome.say: I burned your page unread. The Tithe will have to remember you unwritten.
Who paid half? That question keeps.
We never say welcome. You'll know it anyway.
